chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, who said:

I heard a man ask Abu Al-Hasan Al-Reza (peace be upon him), so he said, 'I treat/work with flour and sell it, and the people say it is not befitting.' So Al-Reza (peace be upon him) said to him, 'And what is wrong with it? Everything that is sold is permissible if the servant fears Allah in it, so there is no problem.'

key_terms.أُعَالِجُ: I treat/work with (in a commercial context)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to sell flour and basic food items in Islam according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) validates the profession of milling and selling flour, a staple commodity, countering those who viewed such trade as beneath a believer's dignity. He establishes that the permissibility hinges on *taqwa* (God-consciousness), emphasizing that honesty and fairness in commercial dealings are the true criteria for acceptability. This reflects the Shia scholarly view that mundane economic activities are acts of worship when performed with integrity and divine awareness.
